question: What minimum capital must a commercial bank maintain under the Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy?

bot_answer:
Under the Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy, a commercial bank must maintain a Minimum Total Capital (MTC) of 9 per cent of the Risk-Weighted Assets (RWAs) on an ongoing basis, which is the Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) [1]. This includes:
- CET1 capital of at least 5.5 per cent of RWAs [1].
- Tier 1 capital of at least 7 per cent of RWAs, with AT1 capital admitted up to 1.5 per cent of RWAs [1].
- Total capital (Tier 1 + Tier 2) of at least 9 per cent of RWAs, with Tier 2 capital admitted up to 2 per cent of RWAs [1].
- A Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB) of 2.5 per cent of RWAs in the form of CET1 capital [3].
expected_answer: Minimum Total Capital (CRAR) of 9 per cent of RWAs, with CET1 capital of at least 5.5 per cent of RWAs.
